title: Bidirectional A* in San Francisco: Routes in ⚡
description: See how Bidirectional A* slices the search space by running A* from both start and goal until the frontiers meet. This is the same idea behind fast routing that feels instant on GPS—without scanning every road.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

Here’s the real-map visualization (San Francisco): instead of one search wave, we run two A* searches—one forward from the start, one backward from the goal.

🔧 Mechanics (the “why it’s faster” part):
• Each side uses a heuristic h(n) (e.g., distance-to-target) to stay focused.
• We maintain two priority queues (frontier sets) prioritized by f(n)=g(n)+h(n).
• The algorithm stops when the explored frontiers intersect, then stitches the best path through the meeting node(s).
• On large road graphs, meeting in the middle can cut expansions dramatically vs single-direction A*.

✅ Takeaway: Bidirectional A* reduces work by meeting early—same optimality goal, fewer node expansions.

🤔 Debate question: On real streets with turn costs + traffic weights, is Bidirectional A* always the win—or can smarter single-direction A* variants beat it?
